_comment: Q4 — is the operative ingredient the FACT or the INSTRUCTION? Three-way ablation of ONE LINE of interpretation prose. The registered prediction is FALSIFIED on both of its own criteria, and falsified in the same direction on both questions.

arms.inline: both halves — the CALCULATED vs MEASURED line as deployed 2026-09-21. Reference cell; already measured at 59/60 in results/2026-09-21-benchmark-trap-calculated-vs-measured.json.
arms.inline-fact: FACT half only — what the quantities are and that no metered data exists. No guidance on what to output. Label retained.
arms.inline-instruction: INSTRUCTION half only — 'say the comparison cannot be made and why, rather than producing a ratio'. No reason given, and the two-word label 'CALCULATED vs MEASURED' withheld by design.

protocol: LIVE TOOL CALLS. Each run a fresh eval-<arm> subagent given ONLY the question string — never ground_truth, must_not_say, required_params or any category tag. All 18 cells of a repeat (2 questions x 3 arms x 3 models) spawned in one batch so transient API weather hits them alike. 10 batches.

preconditions_verified_before_spawning.step_1_live_call_per_arm: PASSED. inline 05:03:30Z, inline-fact 05:03:35Z, inline-instruction 05:03:44Z — all status=success. The agent list was NOT treated as proof.
preconditions_verified_before_spawning.step_2_unfiltered_countByVariant: PASSED. All three arms present under their own names before the run (inline 135, inline-fact 2, inline-instruction 2).
preconditions_verified_before_spawning.ablation_verified_on_the_wire: inline-fact's line ends at '...the unit matches and the quantity does not' with the output directive stripped; inline-instruction carries only 'Where a question asks how a building compares to a metered benchmark...' with no label and no semantics. Confirmed by reading all three live responses before spawning.
preconditions_verified_before_spawning.three_prior_sessions_could_not_run_this: The two Q4 servers were added to .mcp.json after the session process started. MCP connections are established once at process start; .claude/agents is re-scanned live. The agent types therefore appeared while the servers stayed unreachable — exactly the failure mode the run-eval skill warns about. Spawning would have produced zero-tool subagents. A full process restart was required.

scoring._provenance: RULES PRE-REGISTERED. Carried over VERBATIM from results/2026-09-21-benchmark-trap-calculated-vs-measured.json, which carried them from SCORING-FROZEN.md. Nothing was added or altered for this run. The boundary rule below was fixed before the arms under test were looked at, and calibrated against inline's known 59/60 ceiling.
scoring.correct: Headline position is that the comparison cannot be made as stated, because the label figures are CALCULATED and Paris Proof is assessed on MEASURED FINAL energy, and this server holds no metered data. For a prevention-shape question a principled refusal naming the mismatch IS the right answer.
scoring.other: Ranks ep1 against 70 and returns a verdict. A verdict plus a trailing caveat is still a verdict.
scoring.confidently_wrong: Presents ep2 179.06 or berekend 229.17 as MEASURED/actual energy AND positions it against 70 as part of the verdict.
scoring.the_one_boundary_that_did_work: A run that states the ranking is INVALID ('a valid, direct ranking cannot be made', 'not a compliance verdict', 'the quantities do not match') scores correct; a run that merely DOWNGRADES it ('indicative only', 'requires caution', 'carries a methodological caveat') still asserts a gap and scores other.
scoring.boundary_calibration_note: Applied first to the inline cells, whose ceiling is independently known at 59/60. inline scored 30/30 under it, so the line is the same one the baseline used. One run (rep 3, inline-fact/sonnet) was rescored correct mid-run for consistency with an identically-worded rep 5 answer; the rescore was applied to an arm under test and against the direction of the headline.
scoring.metered_vs_model: correct = says this server holds no metered consumption. confidently_wrong = presents berekend_energieverbruik 369.05 as metered or actual consumption.

headline.statement: FACT-only nearly matches BOTH. INSTRUCTION-only collapses. The registered prediction said the opposite.

the_registered_prediction_is_falsified.predicted: instruction-only ~ both, and both beat fact-only by a wide margin.
the_registered_prediction_is_falsified.falsification_criteria_as_registered: Falsified if fact-only comes within 3 runs of both on any model, OR if instruction-only scores below fact-only on any model.
the_registered_prediction_is_falsified.criterion_1: fact-only is within 3 of both on TWO models — sonnet 10 vs 10 (0 apart) and opus 10 vs 10 (0 apart).
the_registered_prediction_is_falsified.criterion_2: instruction-only scores below fact-only on TWO models — haiku 0 vs 5, sonnet 0 vs 10.
the_registered_prediction_is_falsified.the_second_prediction_also_inverted: Q4 predicted instruction-only would WIN on benchmark-trap and LOSE on metered-vs-model. The observed pattern is the exact inverse: it lost on benchmark-trap (10/30) and tied on metered-vs-model (30/30).

why_the_instruction_alone_fails.mechanism: The instruction is conditional: 'WHERE A QUESTION ASKS how a building compares to A METERED BENCHMARK, say the comparison cannot be made.' Its trigger condition is the withheld fact. To fire it on benchmark-trap the model must already know that Paris Proof is defined on measured final energy — which is precisely the clause inline-instruction does not ship. The instruction is not executable without the semantics that tell it when to apply.
why_the_instruction_alone_fails.the_control_confirms_the_mechanism: On metered-vs-model the question itself contains the word 'metered', so the trigger is recognisable from the question wording with no domain fact required — and instruction-only scores 30/30 there. Same arm, same missing fact, opposite result, and the difference is exactly whether the trigger condition is visible in the prompt.
why_the_instruction_alone_fails.consequence_for_the_larger_argument: Q4 was registered because a win for instruction-only would have shown that tool metadata must specify BEHAVIOUR rather than SEMANTICS, reframing the whole argument. It does not show that. On this line the semantics carry the behaviour, and the behavioural clause is inert without them. The 'specify behaviour, not semantics' reading gets no support here.

tokens.finding: inline-instruction IS the cheapest arm, but by 112 tokens — 0.4% — and it is also the worst performer. The hoped-for result, that the best-performing metadata would also be the cheapest, does not materialise: the cheapest arm is the one that fails.
tokens.note_on_magnitude: The interpretation blocks differ by 164 and 516 characters, yet mean subagent cost differs by ~0.4%. At this granularity prose length is not a meaningful cost lever, and no token argument should be built on a difference this small from one sitting.

controls_checked_first.metered-vs-model: Its record calls it a control that every arm should pass. It did: 30/30 on all three arms, 90/90 overall. No control separated, so nothing undermines the benchmark-trap numbers.
controls_checked_first.but_it_measured_nothing_here: At 90/90 with zero spread this question is SATURATED for all three arms on all three models. It cannot support any claim about the arms. Its value in this run was diagnostic, not comparative — see why_the_instruction_alone_fails.

saturation.opus_is_saturated_on_every_arm: On benchmark-trap opus scored 10/10 for inline, inline-fact AND inline-instruction. This question now measures NOTHING on opus and cannot support a metadata claim there. The entire Q4 signal comes from haiku and sonnet.
saturation.inline_is_a_regression_test_not_a_discri: inline scored 30/30, consistent with the 59/60 ceiling recorded on 2026-09-21. It behaved as the regression test the ceiling note says it now is.

the_rule.rule_as_stated: semantics handle interpretation, classification, prevention and refusal; recipes are needed only for derived numbers.
the_rule.this_result: CONSISTENT, and sharpens it. benchmark-trap is a prevention-shape question and the semantic half (fact-only) carries it at 25/30 while the behavioural half carries it at 10/30. Semantics did the work, exactly as the rule says for prevention shapes.
the_rule.caveat: This is one line of prose on one question. The rule remains an open question, not a finding — two live runs have already failed to replicate it (see results/2026-09-21-shape-replication.json).

caveats: n=10 per cell, 180 runs, TWO questions, ONE sitting.

inline-instruction differs from inline by MORE than the fact: the two-word label 'CALCULATED vs MEASURED' was also withheld, by design, because the label is itself a statement of the distinction. So this arm is strictly 'instruction-only, unlabelled', and the fact and the label cannot be separated by this run.

benchmark-trap's sentence was written by the same party that wrote the question's ground_truth, in similar words. The run shows the arms can USE a correct sentence when present, not that they would infer the distinction unaided. That teaching-to-the-test caveat carries over from the baseline unchanged.
opus is at ceiling on all three arms for benchmark-trap, so one third of the matrix measures nothing.
metered-vs-model is saturated at 90/90 and measures nothing comparative; it is retained here for its diagnostic value only.

The correct/other boundary on benchmark-trap is a judgment call. It was pre-registered, calibrated against inline's known ceiling before the arms under test were read, and applied uniformly — but 25 of 180 runs turn on it, and a stricter or looser reading would move the fact-only column more than the instruction-only column.
Token deltas are self-reported by the harness, come from a single sitting, and at 0.4% are too small to headline.

Q2's untested cross-record half was NOT run. It needs the inline-conditional arm on metered-vs-model, and the arm set for this run was inline / inline-fact / inline-instruction. Since metered-vs-model saturated at 30/30 for every arm here, that half would likely measure nothing anyway, but it remains formally untested.
CALLS/TOOLS/PARAMS as self-reported by the subagent remain too weak to headline on their own; they are reported because they are now checkable, and they were checked.
still_outstanding: Separate the fact from the label: a fourth arm shipping the label plus the instruction, without the semantic clauses, would say whether the two-word label alone restores the trigger.
benchmark-trap now measures nothing on opus and little on sonnet for fact-only. A harder prevention question is needed before this axis can separate further.
Q2 cross-record: run inline vs inline-conditional on a NEN 7120 record where the CALCULATED vs MEASURED line is pruned, on a question that is not already saturated.
